cards.text: Abner, the commander of Saul's army, just offered to bring all Israel over to David, and David sent him away in peace (2 Samuel 2:8; 3:21). Just then, David's soldiers and Joab son of Zeruiah get back from a raid with a great plunder (2 Samuel 2:13). But Abner's already gone.

When Joab and his troops arrive, somebody fills him in: Abner son of Ner came to see the king, and the king sent him on his way in peace. Joab walks in carrying a great plunder, and he's not even the headline.

cards.question: Joab hears Abner came and went in peace. Joab goes straight to King David. What does Joab do?

answers.text: Demands to know why David let Abner go
Thanks David for making peace with Abner
Hands David the plunder from the raid

cards.text: Here's Joab, to the king's face: “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you dismiss him? Now he is getting away!” A shiny new stamper took my spot on the counter, and I didn't say ONE word to it.

cards.question: Joab tells King David what Abner was really up to. What does Joab claim Abner came to do?

answers.text: Deceive David and track his movements
Make peace and serve David as king
Challenge Joab to a fight in Hebron

cards.text: As soon as Joab leaves David, he sends messengers after Abner, and they bring him back from the well of Sirah. Abner was already on his way, and now he's headed right back.

cards.question: King David knows Joab sent messengers to bring Abner back.

cards.text: Abner comes back to Hebron. Joab pulls him aside into the gateway, as if to speak to him privately.

cards.question: In the gateway at Hebron, what does Joab do to Abner?
The text tells us why Joab stabs Abner: Abner died on account of the blood of Joab's brother ___.

cards.text: Afterward, the news reaches David. And the king has something to say.

cards.question: When David hears that Joab killed Abner, what does David say about himself and his kingdom?

answers.text: They are forever guiltless before the LORD
They owe Joab their thanks for this
They are safer now that Abner is gone

cards.question: Next, David asks the LORD to forgive Joab and his father's house.

cards.text: Instead, David says may it whirl over the head of Joab and his father's whole house, and may they never be without someone with a discharge or skin disease, someone who leans on a staff, falls by the sword or lacks food. Friend, that is NOT a slap on the wrist.

cards.question: The writer says Joab murdered Abner on his own, with no one else involved.
Joab and his brother Abishai murdered Abner because Abner killed their brother Asahel. Where did Abner kill Asahel?

cards.text: Abner is dead. Now David gives orders to Joab and all the people with him.

cards.question: After Abner's murder, what does King David order Joab and all the people with him to do?

answers.text: Tear their clothes and mourn Abner

cards.text: David's words: “Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” Joab's in that crowd too, and I bet that sackcloth felt REAL heavy on him.

cards.question: King David himself walks behind Abner's funeral bier.

cards.text: They bury Abner in Hebron. The king stands at the tomb.

cards.question: At Abner's tomb in Hebron, what does King David do?

cards.text: Then the king sings a lament for Abner, and it opens with a question: “Should Abner die the death of a fool?”

cards.question: In his lament, David sings that Abner's hands were not bound and his feet were not fettered. So how does David say Abner fell?

answers.text: As a man falls before the wicked
As a soldier falls in battle
As a traitor falls in judgment

cards.text: And all the people weep over Abner even more.
Then the people come and urge David to eat something while it's still day.

cards.question: The people urge David to eat something while it's still day. What does David do?

answers.text: Swears not to eat before sunset
Eats with the people to comfort them
Eats a little to keep his strength

cards.question: The people take note of how David handles Abner's death, and they are unhappy with it.
On that day, all the troops and all Israel were ___ that the king had no part in the murder of Abner.

cards.text: Then the king turns to his servants with a question about the man they just buried.

cards.question: Speaking to his servants, what does King David say has fallen today in Israel?

cards.text: Then David gets honest: he is weak this day, though anointed as king, and the sons of Zeruiah, Joab and his brother Abishai, are too fierce for him (2 Samuel 2:18). Friend, I used to lose arguments to the rubber bands I shared that junk drawer with, so I'm not judging.

cards.question: After saying the sons of Zeruiah are too fierce for him, what does David ask of the LORD?

answers.text: Repay the evildoer according to his evil
Give David the strength to punish them
Show mercy to the sons of Zeruiah

cards.text: We'll set the timer and step away from the oven right here. Friend, this batch isn't out yet.

findings.problem: The joke compares Joab's outburst to Papa Dorin being replaced by a new stamper. That suggests Joab is upset about losing his place to Abner, which the text never says. The passage gives Joab's actual reason: the blood of his brother Asahel (3:27, 30). The joke also makes Papa Dorin look better than Joab ('I didn't say ONE word') instead of making himself the joke.

rule.text: Reasons. He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The right answer 'They are forever guiltless before the LORD' sounds like the Bible. The wrong answers 'They owe Joab their thanks for this' and 'They are safer now that Abner is gone' sound modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Repay the evildoer according to his evil' uses Bible wording. The wrong answers 'Give David the strength to punish them' and 'Show mercy to the sons of Zeruiah' are plain modern wording, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new drawer moment: Papa Dorin losing arguments to the rubber bands. The backstory gives the rubber bands stretching contests, and it's the batteries that argue. Jokes may invent small moments only around his bakery, not add to his drawer backstory.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Cards 9 and 10 are back-to-back bare one-liners ('And all the people weep over Abner even more.' / 'Then the people come and urge David to eat something while it's still day.') with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Card 10's setup is also restated in full by card 11's question, so card 10 adds nothing. Other bare story cards (stop 1 cards 6 and 11, stop 2 cards 1 and 5) have the same thin, voiceless feel.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
